support.passage: In shared autonomy, a critical tension arises when an automated assistant must choose between obeying a human's instruction and deliberately overriding it to prevent harm. This safety-critical behavior is known as intelligent disobedience.

actions.reason: To synthesize the initial formalization of intelligent disobedience and address the project objective.
actions.summary: The Intelligent Disobedience Game (IDG) models interactions between a human leader and an assistive follower as a Stackelberg game. It defines 'intelligent disobedience' as the agent's decision to override human instructions to prevent harm, a necessary evolution from simple compliance. The model identifies 'safety traps' where an agent avoids harm but fails to achieve the human's goal, providing a testbed for learning safe non-compliance.
actions.title: Formalizing Intelligent Disobedience via IDG

proposal.summary: This research entry explores the formalization of 'intelligent disobedience'—a safety-critical behavior where agents must override human commands to prevent harm—using the Intelligent Disobedience Game (IDG) as a foundational framework.
